chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

My father asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was present: 'I lend my garment to a Dhimmi (non-Muslim protected person), and I know that he drinks wine and eats pork, so he returns it to me, and I wash it before I pray in it.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray in it and do not wash it because of that, for you lent it to him and it is pure, and you did not have certainty that he impurified it, so there is no harm in praying in it until you have certainty that he impurified it.'

key_terms.الذِّمِّيّ: A non-Muslim subject living under Islamic rule, granted protection
key_terms.لَحْمُ الْخِنْزِير: Meat of the pig (a primary source of impurity)

ai.seo_question: Is a garment lent to a non-Muslim Muslim ritually pure for prayer if they eat pork or drink wine?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the application of *al-asl al-taharah* (presumption of purity) by distinguishing between mere probability (*zann*) and certainty (*yaqin*) regarding impurity. It establishes that the consumption of impure substances by a Dhimmi does not automatically render their clothing najis, requiring specific evidence of soiling before ritual washing is mandated for prayer validity.
